items.evidence: Recursion is when a function calls itself.
items.note: The student correctly defines recursion as a function calling itself.
The student does not mention a base case or termination condition anywhere.

items.evidence: The function keeps calling itself with a smaller number.
items.note: The student mentions changing the argument, but does not explain that this ensures progress toward a base case.

items.evidence: all the calls share the same stack frame and the same local variables
items.note: The student holds the misconception that recursive calls share a single stack frame and variables.
The student fails to explain stack unwinding or how return values pass back through frames.

items.evidence: it is always faster than using a loop
items.note: The student incorrectly claims recursion is always faster than a loop, holding a known misconception.

target_reason: Introducing a base case is critical to prevent infinite recursion and forms the foundation of all recursive problem-solving.
